one_month_reasoning: Main event in the window: Q3 2026 results. TipRanks lists 29 Oct 2026, after the close, as confirmed, so the 30 Oct close would include the reaction. As of 30 Sep, though, EDGAR had no 8-K or release announcing the date, and last year's Q3 came out in early November. I put roughly 60-65% on the report landing inside the window. Management already told the street what Q3 should look like: NdPr production above 1,000 t, sales flat versus the 1,006 t in Q2, realized oxide price in the high $90s/kg plus about $10/kg of PPA income, and a small drop in PPA income. So a big surprise on the Materials numbers is unlikely. The swing factors are whether GM commercial magnet shipments are confirmed for Q4, the first Dy/Tb output, and capex. Ex-China Dy/Tb prices are very high, which helps the heavy rare earth story. China's suspension of its expanded export controls expires around November, and the news flow before that cuts both ways. The stock fell from about $58 to the mid-$40s in September, then rose about 6% on 30 Sep, so I see no clear momentum signal. I centered the distribution on the current price (median $47.50) and used a 1-month vol of 21% (74%/3.5), widened slightly for earnings. That gives a near-symmetric ladder.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods: (1) 21x EV/EBITDA on 2028E EBITDA of $450M plus net cash at Sep-2027, $43.6; (2) a sum of the parts covering the floor-protected Materials business, Independence magnets, the 10X facility with its DoW EBITDA guarantee, and heavy rare earth optionality, $40.5; (3) CFRA's $850M run-rate EBITDA at 18x, discounted two years at 12%, $55. All three use about 237M fully diluted shares (converts, DoW preferred and DoW warrant all counted as shares).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E adj. EBITDA $450M x 21x = EV $9.45B; plus est. net cash (ex-converts) at Sep-2027 of $0.55B; plus $0.34B warrant exercise proceeds; divided by 237M fully diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Materials: about 5,500-6,000 t NdPr at a $110/kg floor ($115 blended) and ~45% margin, giving ~$300M. Base for this: Q2 Materials EBITDA of $32.5M on 1,006 t, with production above 1,000 t/qtr guided for Q3. Independence magnets 3,000 t/yr capacity, ~$90M. 10X EBITDA guarantee ($140M) partly in place as commissioning starts in 2028, ~$50M. HREE (Dy/Tb, Gd offtake), ~$60M, given ex-China Dy at ~$3,500/kg. Corporate, about -$50M (Q2 was -$11M a quarter).

Set a little below the 23x CFRA uses for its pro forma EBITDA. The 10-year DoW price floor and the 10X offtake cut the downside, which supports a premium to commodity miners, but heavy capex and execution risk keep it below 23x.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash at Sep-2027 (converts treated as equity)
inputs_detail.derivation: Cash and short-term investments of $1.45B at 30 Jun 2026, minus about $187M of non-convertible debt (total long-term debt $934.6M less $747.5M of 2030 notes). Then subtract H2-2026 capex of about $250M (2026 capex guided at $500-600M, $308M spent in H1) and about $650M of 2027 capex, mostly 10X. Add about $200M of operating cash flow and incentives.

178.05M shares outstanding, plus 34.4M from the 2030 notes (conversion price $21.74), 13.32M from the DoW preferred ($30.03) and 11.2M from the DoW warrant ($30.03, $336M of proceeds added back to cash)

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Materials $300M EBITDA x 16x = $4.8B; Independence $90M x 16x = $1.44B; 10X $140M guaranteed EBITDA x 14x = $1.96B less ~$0.4B of capex still to spend after Sep-2027 = $1.56B; HREE optionality $1.5B; corporate -$50M x 12x = -$0.6B; net cash plus warrant proceeds $0.89B. Total about $9.6B / 237M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: From the DoW Offtake Agreement as described in the 10-Q. The facility needs more than $1.25B of capex, partly offset by about $200M of incentives, and commissioning starts in 2028.
Price protection agreement with the DoW, in effect from Oct 2025
Dy/Tb refining starts in H2-2026 and a nine-figure Gd offtake has been signed. Ex-China Dy is around $3,500/kg and Tb around $6,745/kg. I value about $100M of potential EBITDA at 15x.
Discounted from CFRA's 23x because these values are struck before the ramp has happened

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Run-rate EBITDA of $850M (CFRA, reached in 2028-29) x 18x = $15.3B, discounted 2 years at 12% to $12.2B; plus $0.89B net cash and warrant proceeds; divided by 237M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: CFRA's pro forma EBITDA estimate, expected in 2028 or 2029
Cost of equity for a high-beta company with a single site, plus extra for execution risk flagged in the 10-Q risk factors

bear.story: NdPr stays at or below the $110 floor, so the PPA caps both downside and upside. Independence magnet ramp and the GM shipments slip into late 2027, HREE yields disappoint, 10X capex overruns, and China extends the export-control truce so the scarcity premium fades. The stock re-rates toward the DoW's $30 conversion price.

base.story: NdPr runs at about 1,000-1,200 t a quarter with the floor in support. GM magnet shipments start in Q4-26 and ramp through 2027, and first Dy/Tb sales come at ex-China premiums. EBITDA heads toward $250-300M in 2027 while capex keeps free cash flow negative. The multiple holds and the stock goes roughly sideways.

bull.story: China tightens exports again in November 2026 or later, NdPr goes above $130/kg, and heavy rare earth sales scale at $3,000+/kg Dy. Independence reaches 1,000+ t of magnets and more OEM/defense offtakes (Project Swarm) are signed. The market looks through to $850M of EBITDA, back toward the 2025 highs.

thesis_break_reason: At about $30, fully diluted equity value would be about $7B. That is close to what the floor-protected Materials business plus net cash alone is worth, and it matches the $30.03 the DoW paid for its preferred and warrant. A trade there would suggest something fundamental has gone wrong: a failed magnet ramp or lost GM/Apple qualification, a heavy rare earth failure, renegotiation or non-funding of the DoW PPA/offtake, or a large equity raise to fund 10X. Ordinary 74%-vol noise would not explain it.

China's suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls (agreed Nov 2025) comes up for renewal

First shipments of heavy rare earth (Dy/Tb) product from Mountain Pass to Independence
Company can redeem the 2030 converts for cash from this date (if conditions are met); a redemption would force conversion, adding about 34M shares, partly offset by the capped call

key_uncertainties: Path of NdPr prices relative to the $110/kg floor: the PPA cuts the downside, but upside depends on China policy
Execution on the Independence magnet ramp and GM qualification
Heavy rare earth yields and how long ex-China Dy/Tb premiums last
Cost of the 10X facility (>$1.25B) and whether the company needs more capital or the 2030 notes convert
Whether China extends or lets lapse its suspension of export controls in November 2026
Shenghe's ~3% stake possibly passing to China Rare Earth Group (an overhang)
reasoning: Primary-document lane. From the Q2 10-Q and 8-K: NdPr production 840 t (Q1 was a record 917 t; April had planned maintenance) and sales 1,006 t. Materials adjusted EBITDA $32.5M, consolidated $28.5M. PPA income $17.6M, down from $42.3M in Q1 because NdPr prices rose through the $110 floor. Cash and short-term investments $1.45B; debt $935M, mostly 3% converts convertible at $21.74. 2026 capex $500-600M, with H1 free cash flow about -$303M. The DoW holds a preferred and a warrant, both struck at $30.03, which adds about 24.5M shares. The 10X EBITDA guarantee is $140M and commissioning starts in 2028. Footnotes most recaps skip: the 2030 notes became convertible in Q3-26 and are cash-callable from March 2027; the Apple prepayment is booked as non-current deferred revenue with no deliveries before late 2027; the credit agreement requires $500M of minimum cash until EBITDA covenants kick in. On the call, management guided Q3 production above 1,000 t at high-$90s realized pricing plus about $10/kg of PPA income. On value: the floor and DoW contracts make the base business bond-like, but the equity at about $11B fully diluted already prices in a strong ramp. My three methods give $40-55, blended $45.5, about the current price, which is far below the sell-side average target of about $75-78. I treat that gap as optimism to discount, not evidence. On base rates: realized vol is 74%, but the 52-week high came in a 2025 export-control panic, so I used 63% annual vol around a $48 median. I made the lower tail thinner than lognormal because the floor, $1.45B of cash and the DoW's $30 entry price give real support, and kept the right tail fat because of China-driven spikes like the move to $100 in Oct 2025. Research was limited: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and the Twelve Data price-target endpoint was unavailable, so consensus figures come from web aggregators.
